newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sets sale of Food Terminal complex.
newsitem.headline: Manila sets sale of Food Terminal complex.

text.p: The Philippine government is set to sell its 51 percent stake in Food Terminal Inc (FTI) for at least seven billion pesos on June 25, financial advisor Investment Capital Corp of the Philippines (ICCP) said on Tuesday.
FTI operates a 121-hectare agro-industrial complex located at the outskirts of the financial district of Makati.
A total of 44.9 million shares will be sold at a minimum price of 155 pesos per share to a block of investors, Rommel Leuterio, executive vice president of IICP told reporters.
Foreign investors will be allowed to participate in the consortia that will bid for the 51 percent government stake, he said.
The interested groups are expected to be prequalified on May 16.
"We expect FTI to metamorphose into a very competitive commercial area," said FTI president Romeo David, since the site is accessible through major roads.
FTI was incorporated in 1968 to stabilise prices of commodities in the Manila area through an efficient agricultural marketing system.
But it incurred huge losses due to stocks deterioration and high interest costs. Its food retail and wholesale trading operations were phased out in 1989.
Officials said another 14 percent of FTI shares are expected to be sold to small investors after the block sale in June.
